title: The shared document wants OAuth
scenario: A link to a “group project board” asks you to connect your university account and approve permission to read email, files and calendar data. The login page itself is genuine Microsoft/Google.

answers.A: Approve because the login page is genuinely Microsoft/Google, so your password is safe.
answers.B: Do not approve broad permissions; use an approved university tool or ask the sender to share the document normally.
answers.C: Review the app publisher and permissions with university IT before connecting it.

explanation: OAuth scams can use a real provider login screen while asking you to grant a malicious app powerful access.
proTip: A real login page can still authorize a bad app.
